title: Do not re-parse PATH_INFO when validating authenticity token
author: tenderlove

files_changed.patch_snippet:
@@ -381,7 +381,7 @@ def valid_per_form_csrf_token?(token, session) # :doc:
         if per_form_csrf_tokens
           correct_token = per_form_csrf_token(
             session,
-            normalize_action_path(request.fullpath),
+            request.fullpath.chomp("/"),
             request.request_method
           )

@@ -835,6 +835,20 @@ def test_accepts_token_for_correct_path_and_method
     assert_response :success
   end
 
+  def test_rejects_garbage_path
+    get :index
+
+    form_token = assert_presence_and_fetch_form_csrf_token
+
+    assert_matches_session_token_on_server form_token

reasoning: @jeremy authored 7.8% of request_forgery_protection.rb across 5 commits, with first contribution in December 2007. @rafaelfranca's footprint on the same file is 0.6% across 3 commits. @jeremy's last contribution was in 2013; Smart-review still surfaces him because ownership and tenure remain dominant. In practice, a senior consult on a CSRF change would have flagged the path-vs-fullpath interaction.
cost_of_gap: This PR shipped on Jan 10, 2020. Twelve days later a regression was reported on the same PR thread: POST requests with query parameters started failing CSRF validation. The fix landed in #38295, which swapped fullpath for path. A reviewer with deeper history on request_forgery_protection.rb would more likely have flagged the query-string interaction during review.
